lines.trans: Nastya, why do you not eat meat?
Because I am a strict vegetarian.
Really? And here I thought you were Russian.
Vegetarians are people who do not eat meat.
I used to be a vegetarian too.
Really? When did you not eat meat?
In the nineties there was no money at all.
I ate only potatoes for a whole year.
I consider killing animals unacceptable.
But juicy meat cutlets are so tasty!
Every cow has the right to life.
Oh my! You tell stories so beautifully!
I hope you finally understood me.

meanings.en: oh my, goodness (interjection of surprise or admiration)

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.

examples.text: Она балерина, да ещё и вегетарианка!
examples.trans: She's a ballerina, and a vegetarian on top of that!
The bread rings are very tasty.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

meanings.note: after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)
mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.
When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
A cute little cow grazes on the meadow.

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

meanings.note: used when speaking to or about children

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

meanings.note: понял? = got it?; понял = got it

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
Why are we going so slowly?

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.trans: She had a right to the flat.

examples.text: В моей комнате раньше дядя Миша жил.
examples.trans: Uncle Misha used to live in my room.
There used to be an old park here.

meanings.note: also a Russian man (as a noun)

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.
How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: я считаю, что... = I think that...
at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

meanings.note: Убивают! = Murder! Help, they're killing me!

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.
We waited for a whole hour.
There are a lot of people here.

meanings.note: points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
